walkthroughs.body_html:
Your heart fires itself.

The SAN (sinoatrial node) in the right atrium acts as a natural pacemaker — it sends an electrical wave that triggers each heartbeat.

If the SAN fails, doctors fit an artificial pacemaker — a small electrical device under the skin.

Mechanical valves replace leaky natural ones.

Stents prop open arteries narrowed by fatty plaques.

Statins lower blood cholesterol, reducing the chance of clots. For severe failure, a heart transplant may be needed.

Plasma: yellow liquid carrying CO₂, nutrients, wastes and hormones.

Red cells: full of haemoglobin that binds oxygen. White cells: fight pathogens. Platelets: cell fragments that clot wounds.

Arteries have thick muscular walls for high pressure; veins have valves to stop low-pressure backflow.

mcqs.q: Where is the body's natural pacemaker located?
Why do veins have valves but arteries do NOT?
options: Veins carry blood at LOW pressure so backflow is a risk
Veins are thicker so need them
